text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The perennial fuel scarcity, which recently crippled commercial activities in Lagos and environs, is back again with attendant buckpassing between oil marketers and state oil firm NNPC on who is responsible for the problem.
- A road fuel tanker has exploded in Port Harcourt in the southeast killing two persons.

- Military court martial allows an army officer sentenced to 18 months imprisonment for bribe-taking to appeal, which is probably the first appeal allowed under recent reform of the military's justice system.
- Shell oil company's equipment vandalised in troubled oil town of Warri in the midwest.
- Workers in the northern Kaduna state suspend a strike action which led to the sacking of the state's entire workforce.

- Commonwealth leaders seek soft landing for Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha as they end talks with Nigerian dissidents in London without announcing any major decisions or measures against the West African nation.
- Ijaw community leaders and representatives of Shell oil company will now meet to try to resolve a dispute over compensation for an oil spillage in their area 14 years ago.
